name: The Graveyard of Kings
firstVisit: Behind the chapel: the graveyard of the old kings, and of the soldiers who served them.
Every soldier's grave is open. Something is standing among them.

#: The graveyard wall. Low enough to climb, if you wanted to be on the other side of it. Nobody does.
T: A yew. They plant them in graveyards because they live for ever. Somebody thought that would be a comfort.
u: A soldier's grave, empty. The earth isn't sunken in. It's thrown out, all round the edge.
Somebody dug this from the inside.
e: A heap of earth with a spade standing in it. Tomorrow's filling-in.
M: A grassy mound, too neat to be a hill. Something is buried under it, on purpose, with a door.
G: An iron gate, set into the mound and shut fast. No keyhole. No handle on this side.
Carved over it: PUT BACK WHAT THE NIGHT KNOCKED OVER, AND THE DEAD MAY HAVE VISITORS.
In the ground in front of it, three empty sockets.
P: A square socket cut into a flagstone, worn round in the middle. A stone stood here once. It's somewhere else now.
o: A round grave-marker, knocked out of its socket. Heavy, but it would roll if you leaned on it.
c: A candle in an iron lantern, by the chapel door. Somebody keeps it lit for the dead. It does just as well for the living.
V: The Warden's grave, empty. The chain round it has snapped, and the links are bent outwards.

lines: THE MAD KING, OR SO THEY SAY. REST IN PEACE.
Osric Hale. When the queen went missing, he shut himself away, and people said he'd lost his mind.
He named his brother heir, and a month later died of a broken heart. Someone has scratched a small question mark after "heart".
THE BEAUTIFUL QUEEN, OR SO THEY SAY. REST IN PEACE.
No name. The mason left a space for one, and nobody could remember it.
She went missing. They dug her a grave anyway. The earth in front of the stone has never been turned.
THE LOST PRINCE, OR SO THEY SAY. REST IN PEACE.
Lost in the woods. Never found. The stone is smaller than his father's, and kept much tidier.
A great grave, twice as long as the others, and twice as deep. It's empty.
A chain was wound round and round it. The chain has snapped, and the broken links are bent outwards.
The stone says BALDEREK, THE WARDEN. FELL OUT OF THE SKY ONTO A BAKERY. Under it, smaller and in a hurry, someone has carved STAY.
Under that, an older name, scratched out but not quite: AUREK THE TALL.
A SOLDIER OF THE CROWN. The grave below it is open, and empty.
The spade marks go down. The finger marks go up.

objects.name: Mattock
lines: Morning. Mind the holes. I filled them in yesterday.
And the day before. And the day before that.

answer: I fill them in at dusk. I come back at dawn, they're open. The spade's where I left it. What's under it is none of my business.

questions.ask: Have you ever seen what climbs out?
answer: No. I'm in bed by then. I make very sure of it.
Some nights there's a fair bit of walking about. I put the pillow over my head. A man doesn't have to know everything.
Soldiers of the old king's. The crown paid for the stones.
Nobody's paid for the filling-in since. But somebody's got to do it, and I've got the spade.
The old king's crypt. It's been shut since the stones got knocked out of their sockets.
Put them back, if you like. I'm paid for holes, not stones.

questions.ask: Maybe you're just bad at digging.
answer: I'm very good at digging. It's the staying dug I've no say in.
Off you go, then. Mind the holes.

platesLines: With a grind of stone on stone, all three markers settle into their sockets.
In the mound, the iron gate swings inwards on the dark, as if someone down there had been waiting for visitors.
